title: How to Choose a Software Development Agency in the UK: 2026 Guide for Startups and SMEs
metaTitle: How to Choose a Software Development Agency in the UK (2026)
metaDescription: Hiring a UK software or web agency? What to check, UK GDPR and PECR basics, SEIS/EIS and R&D considerations, UK payments and comparing proposals.
excerpt: A UK buyer's guide to hiring a web, MVP, CRM or e-commerce development partner: UK-specific compliance, startup funding considerations, payment methods UK shoppers expect, and how to compare London agencies with remote teams.
altText: UK startup founders reviewing a software development roadmap with a remote engineering team
author: Muhammad Ahmad
authorBio: Muhammad Ahmad is the founder of WebMavien, a web and SaaS development agency. He has 8+ years of experience building React, Next.js and Bubble.io products and has delivered 100+ websites, MVPs and platforms for founders in the UK, USA and UAE.
content:
To choose a software development agency in the UK, look for relevant case studies, senior engineers, a fixed written scope and timeline, full IP transfer to your UK company, and experience with UK GDPR, PECR cookie consent and UK payment methods. Startups should also confirm the agency can document technical work clearly for SEIS/EIS investors and R&D tax relief claims.

:::takeaways
### Key Takeaways
- **London overhead is not the same as quality.** Remote teams that overlap with UK working hours can deliver the same standard with a fixed scope.
- **UK compliance should be built in:** UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018, PECR cookie consent and accessibility.
- **Founders raising SEIS/EIS rounds** need an MVP and documentation that stand up to investor due diligence.
- **UK shoppers expect** card, Apple Pay, Google Pay and buy-now-pay-later options such as Klarna and Clearpay.
:::

## What Should UK Businesses Look For in a Development Agency?

**The same fundamentals apply everywhere, with a few UK-specific checks.** Use this checklist:

| Check | Why It Matters in the UK |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Relevant case studies** | Proves the agency has shipped similar products, not just designed them |
| **Senior engineers named on the project** | Avoids paying senior rates for junior work |
| **Fixed scope, timeline and milestones** | Protects runway and makes budgets predictable |
| **IP assignment to your UK company** | Required by investors and acquirers |
| **UK GDPR and PECR experience** | Avoids costly rework and ICO complaints |
| **Overlap with UK working hours** | Daily communication without late-night calls |
| **Accessibility knowledge (WCAG)** | Supports duties under the Equality Act 2010 and widens your audience |

For a general framework, read [how to choose a web development agency](/blog/how-to-choose-web-development-agency).

## How Do SEIS, EIS and R&D Tax Relief Affect a UK Startup MVP?

**SEIS and EIS make UK startups more attractive to investors, and many founders build their MVP with money raised under these schemes.** Your agency does not decide eligibility, but it can make your life easier:

- **Investor due diligence:** a clean, documented codebase owned by your company makes rounds smoother.
- **Advance assurance:** HMRC's advance assurance process asks about your business plan; a clear product roadmap helps.
- **R&D tax relief:** some software development that resolves technical uncertainty may qualify. Ask your agency for technical documentation of challenges and solutions, and get advice from a qualified accountant.

Always confirm current rules with HMRC guidance and your adviser, as they change. For MVP planning, see our [MVP scoping framework](/blog/startup-mvp-scoping-and-bubble-to-nextjs-migration).

## Should a UK Business Build a Custom CRM or Use HubSpot or Salesforce?

**Small UK teams with standard sales processes are usually best served by HubSpot or Salesforce.** Growing teams with operational workflows, client portals or rising seat costs often save money and time with a custom CRM, provided it is built with UK GDPR controls such as consent tracking, subject access and deletion tools, and audit logs. Compare the options in our [custom CRM vs HubSpot and Salesforce guide](/blog/custom-crm-development-vs-hubspot-salesforce-cost).

## What Do UK E-Commerce Stores Need to Convert?

**UK shoppers expect fast mobile pages, familiar payment methods and clear delivery and returns information.**

:::grid
### Payment Methods
Cards, Apple Pay, Google Pay and PayPal, with buy-now-pay-later options such as Klarna and Clearpay for higher-value baskets.
---
### Delivery and Returns
Clear delivery options with UK carriers, cut-off times and a visible returns policy that meets UK consumer rights.
---
### Speed and SEO
Good Core Web Vitals on mobile and complete Product structured data for Google Shopping and rich results.
:::

Read our [e-commerce checkout and SEO checklist](/blog/ecommerce-seo-and-checkout-conversion-optimization) and [Shopify vs custom Next.js comparison](/blog/shopify-vs-custom-nextjs-ecommerce-2026).

## Which UK Compliance Rules Affect Websites and Software?

:::warning
### Build these in from day one
- **UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018:** lawful basis, privacy notices, data subject rights and security.
- **ICO data protection fee:** most organisations that process personal data must pay it.
- **PECR:** consent before setting non-essential cookies and for most electronic marketing.
- **Consumer protection rules for online sales:** clear pricing, cancellation rights and returns information.
- **Accessibility:** design to WCAG standards to serve all users and support Equality Act duties.
- **FCA rules:** if your product handles payments or credit, use a regulated provider or check whether authorisation is required.
:::

**We run fixed-scope sprints with scheduled overlap with UK working hours, weekly demos and full IP transfer to your UK company.**

:::steps

Workshops to agree the core workflow, acceptance criteria, data model and designs.
---

Engineering of the core product with progress builds shared each week.
---
### Week 3–4: Test, Launch and Hand Over
Testing, UK compliance checks, deployment, analytics and handover of code and accounts.

## Frequently Asked Questions

:::faq
### How do I choose a software development agency in the UK?
Check for relevant case studies, named senior engineers, a fixed written scope and timeline, IP assignment to your company, experience with UK GDPR and PECR, and working hours that overlap with yours. Speak to at least one past client.
### Is it better to hire a London agency or a remote team?
Location matters less than seniority, process and communication. Remote teams that overlap with UK hours and work to a fixed scope can deliver the same quality as London agencies, often with less overhead.
### Does my UK website need a cookie consent banner?
Under PECR, you need consent before setting non-essential cookies such as analytics and advertising cookies. Strictly necessary cookies do not need consent.
### Can software development qualify for UK R&D tax relief?
Some software development can qualify if it seeks an advance in technology by resolving technical uncertainty. Eligibility depends on the specific work, so take advice from a qualified accountant and check HMRC guidance.
### Which payment methods should a UK online store offer?
Most UK stores should offer debit and credit cards, Apple Pay, Google Pay and PayPal, and consider buy-now-pay-later options such as Klarna or Clearpay for higher-value products.
:::

title: How to Choose a SaaS MVP and Software Development Agency in the USA (2026 Guide)

author: Muhammad Ahmad

content:
To choose a SaaS or software development agency in the USA, check for relevant shipped products, senior engineers, a fixed written scope and timeline, full IP assignment to your company, and experience with the compliance your buyers will ask about, such as SOC 2, HIPAA or state privacy laws like the CCPA. Make sure the team overlaps with your time zone for daily communication.

:::takeaways
### Key Takeaways
- **Investors back traction and clean ownership.** Your MVP should ship fast and your company must own all code and IP.
- **Plan for compliance early.** Enterprise buyers often ask for SOC 2; healthcare products need HIPAA safeguards; consumer apps must respect state privacy laws.
- **Time-zone overlap matters more than location.** Agree on core hours that work for EST, CST or PST.
- **Compare agencies on a shared scope,** not on hourly rates.
:::

## What Should US Companies Look For in a Development Agency?

| Check | Why It Matters |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Shipped products similar to yours** | Proves delivery, not just design |
| **Named senior engineers** | Reduces architecture risk and rework |
| **Fixed scope, milestones and timeline** | Keeps burn rate predictable |
| **IP assignment to your US entity** | Required for fundraising and acquisitions |
| **Security and compliance experience** | Speeds up enterprise sales and audits |
| **Overlap with your time zone** | Enables daily stand-ups and fast decisions |

Our general framework is in [how to choose a web development agency](/blog/how-to-choose-web-development-agency).

## How Do You Build an Investor-Ready SaaS MVP?

**An investor-ready MVP shows real usage, runs on a maintainable stack and is fully owned by the company.** In practice that means:

:::steps
### Scope Around One Paying Workflow
Launch the smallest product that proves customers will pay. Use our [MVP scoping framework](/blog/startup-mvp-scoping-and-bubble-to-nextjs-migration).
---
### Use a Mainstream, Hireable Stack
React and Next.js, PostgreSQL and Stripe are familiar to investors' technical advisers and easy to hire for.
---
### Instrument Everything
Analytics, activation metrics and revenue data from day one give you the numbers investors ask for.
---
### Keep Ownership Clean
All code, accounts and IP sit with your company, with contributor agreements in place.
:::

For AI products, follow our [21-day AI SaaS MVP blueprint](/blog/how-to-build-ai-saas-mvp-in-21-days).

## Why Are US Mid-Market Companies Building Custom CRMs?

**Because per-seat licences and add-on tools grow with every hire, and standard CRM objects rarely fit operational workflows.** Companies with bookings, field operations, partner networks or client portals often get better results from a custom CRM that syncs with their existing tools. See the [custom CRM vs HubSpot and Salesforce comparison](/blog/custom-crm-development-vs-hubspot-salesforce-cost).

## How Do SOC 2, HIPAA and the CCPA Affect Software Architecture?

**Compliance is far cheaper to design in than to retrofit.**

:::grid
### SOC 2
An attestation framework from the AICPA covering security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality and privacy. Build in access controls, audit logs, encryption, change management and monitoring early.
---
### HIPAA
Applies to protected health information handled by covered entities and their business associates. Requires administrative, physical and technical safeguards, and business associate agreements with vendors.
---
### CCPA / CPRA and State Privacy Laws
California and a growing number of states give consumers rights to know, delete and opt out. Your product needs request handling and clear data inventories.
---
### Accessibility (ADA)
US businesses face accessibility expectations and lawsuits over inaccessible websites. Design to WCAG standards from the start.
:::

:::warning
### Check vendor agreements too
Your hosting, analytics, email and AI providers process your users' data. For HIPAA workloads, use only vendors that sign business associate agreements, and avoid sending protected data to services that do not.
:::

## Headless Next.js or Shopify Plus for US E-Commerce?

**Shopify Plus suits brands that want a managed platform; headless or custom Next.js suits brands that need performance, SEO control and complex B2B or subscription logic.** Read [Shopify vs custom Next.js](/blog/shopify-vs-custom-nextjs-ecommerce-2026) for the full comparison, and remember US sales tax rules for marketplaces and multi-state sellers.

:::faq
### How do I choose a SaaS development agency in the USA?
Look for shipped products similar to yours, senior engineers named on your project, a fixed scope and timeline, IP assignment to your company, experience with the compliance your buyers require, and working hours that overlap with your time zone.
### Does my SaaS need SOC 2 compliance?
Not to launch, but many enterprise buyers request a SOC 2 report during procurement. Building access controls, logging, encryption and change management into your MVP makes a later audit much easier.

HIPAA compliance involves administrative, physical and technical safeguards for protected health information, such as access controls, audit logs and encryption, plus business associate agreements with vendors that handle the data.

Yes. What matters is seniority, a clear scope, time-zone overlap for communication and a contract that assigns all IP to your US company.

authorBio: Muhammad Ahmad is the founder of WebMavien, a web and SaaS development agency. He has 8+ years of experience building React, Next.js and Bubble.io products and has delivered 100+ websites, MVPs and platforms for founders in the UK, USA and UAE.
content:
When hiring a web, e-commerce or CRM developer in Dubai or the UAE, look for proven bilingual Arabic and English (right-to-left) builds, experience integrating UAE payment methods such as Apple Pay, Tabby and Tamara, WhatsApp-first customer workflows, and knowledge of UAE data protection rules: the federal PDPL onshore, and the DIFC and ADGM regimes in those free zones.

:::takeaways
### Key Takeaways
- **True bilingual means more than translation.** Arabic needs right-to-left layouts, Arabic typography and localised content and SEO.
- **UAE shoppers expect** Apple Pay, cards and buy-now-pay-later options such as Tabby and Tamara.
- **WhatsApp is the main sales channel** for many UAE businesses, so CRMs should be built around it.
- **Data protection depends on where you operate:** onshore UAE, DIFC or ADGM each have their own rules.
:::

## What Should UAE Businesses Look For in a Development Partner?

| Check | Why It Matters in the UAE |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Bilingual Arabic and English portfolio** | RTL done badly looks broken to Arabic-speaking customers |
| **Local payment integrations** | Checkout must support the methods UAE shoppers use |
| **WhatsApp Business Platform experience** | Most enquiries and follow-ups happen on WhatsApp |
| **Data protection knowledge** | Onshore, DIFC and ADGM rules differ |
| **Fixed scope and timeline** | Predictable delivery for launches tied to seasons and events |
| **Working-hours overlap with Gulf Standard Time** | Fast communication during the UAE working week |

## How Do You Build a True Bilingual Arabic and English Website?

**Build bilingual support into the architecture rather than bolting on a translation plugin.**

:::steps
### Use Right-to-Left Layouts Properly
Set `dir="rtl"` and `lang="ar"` on Arabic pages, use CSS logical properties so spacing and alignment flip automatically, and mirror icons that indicate direction.
---
### Choose Arabic-Friendly Typography
Use fonts designed for Arabic script with matching weights for English, and test line heights for both languages.
---
### Localise, Do Not Just Translate
Write Arabic content for local customers, including product names, calls to action and dates, rather than relying on machine translation.
---
### Set Up Bilingual SEO
Use separate URLs for each language (for example `/ar/` and `/en/`), hreflang tags, localised metadata and Arabic keyword research.
:::

## Which Payment Methods Do UAE Online Shoppers Expect?

**Offer cards, Apple Pay and Google Pay, and consider buy-now-pay-later options such as Tabby and Tamara for higher-value baskets.** Many stores also offer cash on delivery, although reducing it over time lowers failed deliveries. Payment gateways commonly used in the UAE include Stripe, Checkout.com, Network International, PayTabs and Telr; the right choice depends on your business licence, settlement needs and the payment methods you want to offer.

For checkout best practices that apply in every market, see our [e-commerce checkout and SEO checklist](/blog/ecommerce-seo-and-checkout-conversion-optimization).

## Why Do Dubai Businesses Need WhatsApp-First CRMs?

**Because customers in the UAE expect to enquire, negotiate and book through WhatsApp, and standard CRMs treat it as an add-on.**

:::grid
### Real Estate Brokerages
Capture leads from property portals and ads, route them to agents, log every WhatsApp conversation and track viewings and offers.
---
### Clinics and Wellness Brands
Booking, reminders, follow-ups and patient communication in one place, with access controls for sensitive information.
---
### Luxury and Service Brands
Personal client histories, preferences and order tracking, shared across the team instead of stored on staff phones.
:::

A custom CRM connected to the WhatsApp Business Platform keeps every conversation attached to the customer record. Read [7 signs you need a custom CRM](/blog/when-to-build-custom-crm-workflows-automation) and the [custom CRM vs HubSpot and Salesforce comparison](/blog/custom-crm-development-vs-hubspot-salesforce-cost).

## Which UAE Data Protection and Tax Rules Affect Your Platform?

:::warning
### Know which regime applies to you
- **Federal Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL):** applies to processing personal data in the UAE outside the financial free zones.
- **DIFC Data Protection Law:** applies to businesses operating in the Dubai International Financial Centre.
- **ADGM Data Protection Regulations:** apply to businesses in Abu Dhabi Global Market.
- **Sector rules:** health data and financial services have additional requirements.
- **VAT and corporate tax:** your invoices, receipts and reports must support UAE VAT requirements, and the UAE is introducing e-invoicing. Confirm the current requirements with your tax adviser.
:::

## Frequently Asked Questions

:::faq
### How do I build an Arabic and English website?
Build both languages into the architecture: right-to-left layouts with `dir="rtl"` and CSS logical properties, Arabic-friendly fonts, professionally localised content, separate language URLs and hreflang tags for SEO.
### Which payment gateways work in the UAE?
Commonly used options include Stripe, Checkout.com, Network International, PayTabs and Telr, with buy-now-pay-later providers such as Tabby and Tamara. The best fit depends on your licence, settlement needs and payment methods.
### Do Dubai businesses need a WhatsApp CRM?
Many do, because customers prefer to enquire and book through WhatsApp. A CRM connected to the WhatsApp Business Platform keeps conversations, leads and bookings in one shared record.

Most onshore businesses fall under the federal PDPL. Businesses in DIFC follow the DIFC Data Protection Law, and businesses in ADGM follow the ADGM Data Protection Regulations. Sector-specific rules may also apply.

title: How Much Does It Cost to Build a SaaS Application? The 7 Factors That Decide Your Budget
metaTitle: SaaS Development Cost in 2026: 7 Factors That Decide It
metaDescription: What really drives SaaS development cost in 2026? Product tier, multi-tenancy, billing, AI, integrations, stack and team model, explained by SaaS engineers.
excerpt: SaaS budgets are decided by seven factors, not by a page count. Learn which features add the most engineering effort, how stack and team model change cost, and how to scope a SaaS MVP you can afford.
tags: how much does it cost to build a saas
altText: SaaS product planning board showing feature scope, billing and infrastructure cost drivers
author: Muhammad Ahmad
authorBio: Muhammad Ahmad is the founder of WebMavien, a web and SaaS development agency. He has 8+ years of experience building React, Next.js and Bubble.io products and has delivered 100+ websites, MVPs and platforms for founders in the UK, USA and UAE.
content:
The cost of building a SaaS application is decided by seven factors: product tier, number of core workflows, multi-tenancy and permissions, billing complexity, AI features, third-party integrations, and the stack and team model you choose. Two products with the same number of screens can differ in effort by several times because of these factors alone.

:::takeaways
### Key Takeaways
- **Scope drives cost, not screens.** Multi-tenancy, billing logic, AI pipelines and integrations add far more engineering effort than extra pages.
- **Three product tiers cover most SaaS builds:** a single-workflow micro-SaaS, a multi-tenant B2B platform, and an AI-enabled or enterprise SaaS. Each tier is roughly a step up in effort.
- **Your stack changes cost twice.** Bubble.io is usually faster to launch; React and Next.js usually cost less to scale and are easier to hand to investors and new engineers.
- **Budget for what happens after launch.** Hosting, databases, AI tokens, monitoring and iteration sprints are recurring costs that most first quotes leave out.
:::

## What Are the Three Tiers of SaaS Product (and How Do They Differ in Effort)?

**Most SaaS products fall into one of three tiers, and the tier sets the baseline effort before any custom feature is added.** Identifying your tier first is the fastest way to get a realistic quote from any agency.

| SaaS Tier | Typical Scope | Typical Timeline | Relative Effort |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Micro-SaaS / Single-Workflow MVP** | Sign-up and login, one core workflow, Stripe checkout, basic admin view | 3–4 weeks | Low |
| **Multi-Tenant B2B SaaS** | Organisations and teams, role-based permissions, subscriptions with plan limits, onboarding, audit logs | 4–8 weeks | Medium |
| **AI-Enabled or Enterprise SaaS** | Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), structured AI workflows, usage-based billing, SSO, compliance controls | 6–12 weeks | High |

A **micro-SaaS** solves one painful job for one type of user. A **multi-tenant B2B SaaS** lets many companies share one application while keeping their data strictly separated. An **AI-enabled SaaS** adds model orchestration, vector search and token cost management on top of the B2B foundation.

:::tip
### Scope the tier, then the features
Founders often ask for a quote on a feature list. Agencies give more accurate estimates when you first state the tier ("a multi-tenant B2B tool for agencies"), then list the three workflows a paying customer must complete on day one.
:::

## Which Features Increase SaaS Engineering Cost the Fastest?

**Five features add effort out of proportion to how small they look on a wireframe: multi-tenancy, billing, permissions, AI and integrations.** Each one brings edge cases, security requirements and testing that a simple page does not.

:::grid
### Multi-Tenancy and Data Isolation
Every query must be scoped to the right organisation. Getting this wrong causes cross-customer data leaks, so it needs careful schema design, tests and often database-level row security. See our [multi-tenant SaaS architecture guide](/blog/multi-tenant-saas-stripe-billing-architecture).
---
### Subscription Billing
Trials, upgrades, downgrades, proration, failed payments and cancellations all need to stay in sync with Stripe through webhooks. Usage-based or seat-based billing adds more logic.
---
### Roles and Permissions
Owner, admin, member and read-only roles, plus invitations and seat limits, touch almost every screen and API route in the product.
---
### AI Features
Retrieval pipelines, prompt orchestration, structured outputs, evaluation and token cost controls are real engineering work. Read [AI wrapper vs defensible AI SaaS](/blog/ai-wrapper-vs-defensible-ai-saas-2026) before scoping them.
---
### Third-Party Integrations
Each CRM, calendar, accounting or messaging integration adds authentication, rate limits, error handling and ongoing maintenance when the vendor changes its API.
:::

Features that usually add **less** effort than founders expect include marketing pages, static dashboards, email notifications built on a transactional email provider, and file uploads to managed cloud storage.

## How Do Agency Type and Location Change SaaS Development Cost?

**The delivery model matters as much as geography.** A large onshore consultancy, a solo freelancer and a fixed-scope product studio will quote very different amounts for the same scope because they carry different overheads and risks.

| Delivery Model | Strengths | Risks to Budget |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Large onshore consultancy** (London, New York, San Francisco, Dubai) | Process, account management, enterprise procurement | Highest overhead, long discovery phases, hourly billing that rewards slow delivery |
| **Freelancer or small offshore team** | Lowest hourly rates, flexible | Quality varies widely, single point of failure, weak architecture on complex SaaS |
| **Fixed-scope product studio** | Senior engineers, defined deliverables, predictable timeline | Requires a tightly scoped first release; scope changes become new milestones |
| **In-house hiring** | Long-term ownership, deep product knowledge | Months of recruiting before the first line of code; full salary and benefits |

For founders who want an outcome rather than hours, a fixed-scope model removes the biggest source of budget overruns: open-ended time and materials billing. Our guide on [how to choose a web development agency](/blog/how-to-choose-web-development-agency) covers how to compare these models fairly.

## Does Choosing Bubble.io or React and Next.js Change the Cost?

**Yes. Bubble.io usually lowers the cost of the first release, while React and Next.js usually lower the cost of growth.** The right choice depends on whether speed to validation or long-term scalability matters more for your next 12 months.

- **Choose Bubble.io** when you need to validate a workflow quickly, organic search traffic is not your main channel, and your user volume will stay modest while you test demand.
- **Choose React and Next.js** when SEO, performance, complex permissions, heavy data processing or investor technical due diligence are part of your plan.

We compare both in detail, including total cost of ownership over three years, in [React / Next.js vs Bubble.io for your SaaS MVP](/blog/react-vs-bubble-io-for-saas-mvp-2026).

## What Are the Hidden Running Costs After a SaaS Launches?

**A SaaS product has ongoing costs that start the day you launch, and most first quotes do not include them.** Plan for these line items from day one:

:::steps
### Hosting and Databases
Application hosting, a managed database, backups and file storage. These grow with users and data volume.
---
### AI and API Usage
Language model tokens, embeddings, and paid third-party APIs are billed per use. Without caching and limits, a few heavy users can erode your margin.
---
### Monitoring and Security
Error tracking, uptime monitoring, logging and dependency updates keep the product stable and reduce security exposure.
---
### Iteration Sprints
The first release teaches you what customers actually want. Budget for regular improvement sprints after launch rather than treating the MVP as finished.
:::

:::warning
### Watch for open-ended retainers
A low upfront quote attached to a mandatory monthly retainer can cost more over a year than a clearly scoped build. Always ask what is included after launch, what is optional, and who owns the code.
:::

## How Can You Reduce SaaS Development Cost Without Cutting Quality?

**Cut scope, not engineering standards.** The cheapest SaaS is the one that ships the smallest set of features a customer will pay for, built on an architecture that does not need to be rewritten.

1. **Define one paying workflow.** Write down the single job a customer completes that justifies paying. Everything else goes to version two. Our [MVP scoping framework](/blog/startup-mvp-scoping-and-bubble-to-nextjs-migration) shows how to sort must-haves from nice-to-haves.
2. **Use managed services.** Authentication, payments, email and file storage are solved problems. Integrate them instead of building them.
3. **Get the data model right first.** Multi-tenancy and permissions are expensive to retrofit. Design them into the first release.
4. **Fix the scope before you fix the price.** Ask agencies for a written scope with acceptance criteria, then compare quotes on the same document.

### What is the biggest factor in SaaS development cost?
The biggest factor is scope complexity, especially multi-tenancy, subscription billing, permissions, AI features and integrations. These add more engineering effort than the number of screens or pages.
### How long does it take to build a SaaS MVP?
A focused single-workflow SaaS MVP typically takes 3 to 4 weeks with a senior team. A multi-tenant B2B platform takes around 4 to 8 weeks, and an AI-enabled or enterprise SaaS takes around 6 to 12 weeks, depending on integrations and compliance needs.
### Is it cheaper to build a SaaS with no-code tools like Bubble.io?
Bubble.io is usually cheaper and faster for the first release. As usage, SEO needs and data complexity grow, platform usage fees and performance limits can make custom React and Next.js code cheaper to run and scale.
### What ongoing costs should I budget for after launching a SaaS?
Budget for hosting and databases, AI and third-party API usage, monitoring and security tooling, and regular iteration sprints. These costs scale with users and should be planned before launch.

Prepare a one-page brief that states your product tier, target customer, the three workflows a paying customer must complete, required integrations and any compliance needs. Agencies can then quote against the same scope, which makes quotes comparable.

title: How to Build a Multi-Tenant SaaS with Stripe Billing and Role-Based Permissions
metaTitle: Multi-Tenant SaaS Architecture with Stripe Billing & RBAC
metaDescription: A practical guide to multi-tenant SaaS: tenant data isolation, row-level security, idempotent Stripe webhooks, plan entitlements and role-based access.
excerpt: A production blueprint for B2B SaaS teams: choosing a tenancy model, enforcing data isolation, keeping Stripe subscriptions in sync with webhooks, and designing roles and permissions that scale.
altText: Diagram of a multi-tenant SaaS architecture with organisations, roles and Stripe subscription webhooks
author: Muhammad Ahmad
authorBio: Muhammad Ahmad is the founder of WebMavien, a web and SaaS development agency. He has 8+ years of experience building React, Next.js and Bubble.io products and has delivered 100+ websites, MVPs and platforms for founders in the UK, USA and UAE.
content:
A multi-tenant SaaS serves many customer organisations from one application while keeping each organisation's data isolated. A production-ready setup needs three things: a tenancy model enforced on every query, Stripe subscriptions kept in sync through verified, idempotent webhooks, and role-based access control (RBAC) checked on the server, never only in the UI.

:::takeaways
### Key Takeaways
- **Start with a shared database and a tenant ID on every row.** It is the simplest model to run, and row-level security can enforce isolation at the database layer.
- **Treat Stripe as the source of truth for billing,** and your database as a cached copy updated only by verified webhooks.
- **Make every webhook handler idempotent.** Stripe can deliver the same event more than once and not always in order.
- **Check permissions on the server for every request.** Hiding a button is a user-experience choice, not a security control.
:::

## What Is Multi-Tenancy in SaaS?

**Multi-tenancy is an architecture in which a single application and infrastructure serve multiple customers (tenants), with each tenant's data logically or physically separated.** In B2B SaaS, a tenant is usually an organisation or workspace, and users belong to one or more tenants.

There are three common tenancy models:

| Tenancy Model | How It Works | Best For | Trade-offs |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Shared database, shared schema** | Every table has a `tenant_id` column; queries filter by it | Most startups and SMB-focused SaaS | Simplest and cheapest to run; isolation depends on discipline or row-level security |
| **Shared database, schema per tenant** | Each tenant gets its own schema in one database | Mid-market SaaS needing stronger separation | More complex migrations across many schemas |
| **Database per tenant** | Each tenant has a dedicated database | Enterprise or regulated customers | Highest isolation and cost; harder to operate at scale |

## How Should a Startup Enforce Tenant Data Isolation?

**Use a shared schema with a required tenant ID, and enforce it in two places: the application layer and the database layer.** Relying on developers to remember a `WHERE tenant_id = ?` clause on every query is how cross-tenant leaks happen.

:::steps
### Add a tenant ID to every tenant-owned table
Make the column `NOT NULL`, index it, and include it in composite unique constraints (for example, a project slug must be unique per tenant, not globally).
---
### Resolve the tenant once per request
Derive the active tenant from the authenticated session or subdomain in middleware, verify the user is a member, and pass a tenant context to all data access functions.
---
### Enforce isolation in the database
In PostgreSQL, enable row-level security (RLS) policies that compare each row's tenant ID with a session setting. If application code forgets a filter, the database still refuses to return other tenants' rows.
---
### Test for leaks explicitly
Write automated tests that sign in as a user from tenant A and attempt to read, update and delete tenant B's records through every API route.
:::

:::warning
### Background jobs bypass your middleware
Cron jobs, queue workers and admin scripts often run outside the request context. Pass the tenant ID explicitly to every job and apply the same scoped data access layer, or they become the most likely source of a data leak.
:::

## How Do You Keep Stripe Subscriptions in Sync with Your App?

**Treat Stripe as the source of truth for billing state and update your database only from verified webhook events.** Never grant or remove access based on what the browser reports after checkout.

These are the four pillars of reliable Stripe billing architecture:

:::grid
### 1. Verify Every Webhook Signature
Use the endpoint's signing secret to verify the `Stripe-Signature` header against the raw request body before processing anything. Reject events that fail verification.
---
### 2. Make Handlers Idempotent
Store each processed event ID and skip duplicates. Stripe may retry deliveries and does not guarantee event order, so handlers should fetch the latest object state when order matters.
---
### 3. Map Subscriptions to Tenants
Store the Stripe customer ID and subscription ID on the tenant record, not on an individual user, so billing survives when the original admin leaves the company.
---
### 4. Derive Entitlements From Plan Data
Keep a plan-to-features map (seats, projects, API limits) in your code or database. Check entitlements on the server rather than scattering plan names through the codebase.
:::

The webhook events most B2B SaaS products handle first are `checkout.session.completed`, `customer.subscription.created`, `customer.subscription.updated`, `customer.subscription.deleted`, `invoice.paid` and `invoice.payment_failed`. Together they cover sign-up, plan changes, cancellations, renewals and failed payments.

:::tip
### Respond fast, process later
Return a 2xx response to Stripe quickly after verifying and storing the event, then process heavy work in a background job. Slow handlers cause timeouts and retries, which multiply duplicate events.
:::

## How Should Role-Based Access Control Work in a B2B SaaS?

**Define a small set of roles per tenant, map each role to explicit permissions, and check permissions on the server for every action.** Most B2B products start well with four roles.

| Role | Typical Permissions |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Owner** | Everything, including billing, deleting the workspace and transferring ownership |
| **Admin** | Manage members, roles and settings; no billing ownership transfer |
| **Member** | Create and edit the core records of the product |
| **Viewer** | Read-only access, often used for clients or stakeholders |

Store membership as a join between users and tenants with a role on each membership, so one person can be an admin in one workspace and a viewer in another. Check permissions (for example `project.delete`) rather than role names in your code; that lets you add custom roles later without rewriting every check.

## What Should Day-One Tenant Onboarding Include?

**A new customer should go from sign-up to their first useful result in one session.** A good onboarding flow creates the workspace, assigns the creator as owner, starts a trial or checkout, invites teammates and seeds example data so the product never opens empty.

1. Create the tenant and owner membership in a single database transaction.
2. Create the Stripe customer and attach it to the tenant.
3. Start a trial or send the user to Stripe Checkout for the selected plan.
4. Prompt for teammate invites with a role picker.
5. Seed sample records or a guided checklist so the first screen demonstrates value.

Building this foundation correctly is a large part of what separates a demo from a sellable product. If you are still deciding on scope and budget, read [what drives SaaS development cost](/blog/saas-application-development-cost-2026). For AI products built on this foundation, see [how to build an AI SaaS MVP in 21 days](/blog/how-to-build-ai-saas-mvp-in-21-days).

:::casestudy

## Frequently Asked Questions

:::faq
### What is the best multi-tenant database model for a startup SaaS?
For most startups, a shared database with a shared schema and a tenant ID on every row is best. It is the simplest and cheapest to operate, and PostgreSQL row-level security can enforce isolation at the database layer.
### How do I prevent one customer from seeing another customer's data?
Resolve the tenant from the authenticated session on every request, scope all queries through a single data access layer, enable row-level security in the database, and write automated tests that try to access another tenant's records.
### Why do Stripe webhooks need to be idempotent?
Stripe can deliver the same event more than once and does not guarantee delivery order. Recording processed event IDs and skipping duplicates prevents double upgrades, duplicate emails and incorrect billing state.
### Should Stripe subscriptions belong to users or organisations?
In B2B SaaS, subscriptions should belong to the organisation (tenant). That keeps billing intact when the person who signed up leaves the company and makes seat-based pricing straightforward.
### How many roles should a B2B SaaS start with?
Four roles (owner, admin, member and viewer) cover most early B2B products. Check permissions instead of role names in code so you can add custom roles later without a rewrite.
:::

title: AI Wrapper vs Defensible AI SaaS: How to Build AI Products Customers Keep Paying For
metaTitle: AI Wrapper vs Defensible AI SaaS: What Makes AI Stick
metaDescription: Why thin ChatGPT wrappers churn, and the four layers (proprietary data, workflows, integrations, unit economics) that make an AI SaaS defensible.
excerpt: Thin AI wrappers lose users the moment a general chatbot can do the same job. Here are the four engineering layers that turn an AI feature into a product with retention, margins and a moat.
breadcrumbTitle: AI Wrapper vs Defensible AI SaaS
tags: how to build a defensible ai startup
altText: Layered diagram of a defensible AI SaaS stack with retrieval, workflows, integrations and cost controls
author: Muhammad Ahmad
authorBio: Muhammad Ahmad is the founder of WebMavien, a web and SaaS development agency. He has 8+ years of experience building React, Next.js and Bubble.io products and has delivered 100+ websites, MVPs and platforms for founders in the UK, USA and UAE.
content:
An AI wrapper is a product that sends a user's input to a general-purpose language model and returns the answer with little added value. A defensible AI SaaS combines the model with four layers a general chatbot cannot easily copy: the customer's own context, structured multi-step workflows, deep integrations with the tools they already use, and unit economics that stay profitable as usage grows.

:::takeaways
### Key Takeaways
- **Wrappers compete with free.** If a user can paste the same prompt into ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini and get a similar answer, your product has no reason to exist.
- **Proprietary context is the strongest moat.** Retrieval over the customer's own documents, history and data produces answers no general assistant can.
- **Workflows beat chat.** Products that complete a job end to end (extract, decide, write back, notify) retain users far better than a text box.
- **Token costs must be engineered, not hoped for.** Caching, model routing and usage limits protect gross margin as you scale.
:::

## What Is the Difference Between an AI Wrapper and a Defensible AI SaaS?

**The difference is where the value lives.** In a wrapper, nearly all the value comes from the underlying model, which your competitors and your customers can access directly. In a defensible AI SaaS, the value comes from what you build around the model.

| Dimension | AI Wrapper | Defensible AI SaaS |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Input** | A free-text prompt | Customer data, documents, records and events |
| **Output** | Unstructured text to copy and paste | Structured results written back into the user's systems |
| **Interface** | A chat box | A workflow tied to a business process |
| **Switching cost** | None: users can leave in minutes | High: history, integrations and team habits live in the product |
| **Model dependency** | Breaks or becomes redundant when the model provider ships the same feature | Swaps models freely; the value sits in data and workflow |

## What Are the Four Engineering Layers of a Defensible AI Product?

**Defensible AI products are built in layers, and each layer makes the product harder to replace.** You do not need all four on day one, but your MVP should include at least the first two.

:::steps
### Layer 1: Proprietary Context With Retrieval
Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) fetches relevant passages from the customer's own data (documents, tickets, contracts, product catalogues) and gives them to the model with each request. Answers become specific, verifiable and tied to the customer's business. A vector database such as pgvector inside PostgreSQL is often enough for an MVP.
---
### Layer 2: Structured, Multi-Step Workflows
Instead of returning prose, the product asks the model for structured output (for example JSON that matches a schema), validates it, and uses it to take the next step: create a record, route a ticket, draft a reply for approval. Validation and retries make results reliable enough for real work.
---
### Layer 3: Deep Integrations
Reading from and writing back to CRMs, help desks, accounting tools, calendars and messaging apps puts the AI inside the user's daily workflow. Every integration adds switching cost.
---
### Layer 4: Unit Economics and Cost Controls
Cache repeated requests, route simple tasks to smaller, cheaper models, cap usage per plan, and track cost per customer. Pricing tiers should reflect real model usage so heavy users do not erase your margin.
:::

:::warning
### Do not build your moat on a prompt
Prompts are easy to copy and model providers regularly ship features that make prompt-only products redundant. Treat prompts as configuration; invest your engineering time in data, workflow and integrations.
:::

## How Do You Know If Your AI Product Is Just a Wrapper?

**Ask whether a customer could get 80% of the value by pasting their request into a general AI assistant.** If the answer is yes, you are building a wrapper. Other warning signs include:

- Users copy results out of your product and into another tool.
- Your product has no memory of the customer's past work or data.
- A new model release from a major provider overlaps with your core feature.
- Usage spikes at sign-up and drops sharply after the first few weeks.

## How Long Does It Take to Build a Defensible AI SaaS MVP?

**A focused AI SaaS MVP with retrieval, one structured workflow, one integration and billing can be built in around 3 to 4 weeks by a senior team.** The key is to pick one painful, repeated job and automate it end to end rather than adding many shallow AI features.

Our week-by-week plan is in [how to build an AI SaaS MVP in 21 days](/blog/how-to-build-ai-saas-mvp-in-21-days). If your product will serve multiple companies, design for tenant isolation from the start using our [multi-tenant SaaS architecture guide](/blog/multi-tenant-saas-stripe-billing-architecture).

:::casestudy

## Frequently Asked Questions

:::faq
### What is an AI wrapper?
An AI wrapper is a software product that mainly passes user input to a third-party large language model and returns the response, adding little proprietary data, workflow or integration. Because users can access the same model directly, wrappers usually struggle with retention.
### Can an AI wrapper become a real business?
Yes, if it adds layers that a general assistant cannot copy: retrieval over the customer's own data, structured workflows that complete a job, integrations with existing tools, and pricing aligned with model costs.
### What is RAG and why does it matter for AI SaaS?
Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) retrieves relevant information from a knowledge source, such as a customer's documents, and supplies it to the language model with the request. It makes answers more accurate and specific, and it ties the product's value to data competitors do not have.
### How do AI SaaS companies control token costs?
They cache repeated requests, route simple tasks to smaller models, limit context to the most relevant retrieved passages, set usage caps per plan, and monitor cost per customer so pricing reflects actual usage.
### Should an AI startup use OpenAI, Anthropic or open-source models?
Design the product so models can be swapped. Many teams use a strong hosted model for complex reasoning and a smaller or cheaper model for simple steps, then re-evaluate as models and prices change.

title: MVP Development Agency for Startups: How to Launch a Revenue-Ready MVP in 21 Days
metaTitle: MVP Development Agency for Startups: Launch in 21 Days
metaDescription: How to choose an MVP development agency: agency vs freelancer vs in-house, how a 21-day MVP process works, and five questions to ask before you sign.
excerpt: What a good MVP development agency actually does, how it compares with freelancers and in-house hires, how a fixed 21-day build works, and the questions that protect founders before signing.
altText: Startup founders reviewing an MVP launch plan with a development agency
author: Muhammad Ahmad
authorBio: Muhammad Ahmad is the founder of WebMavien, a web and SaaS development agency. He has 8+ years of experience building React, Next.js and Bubble.io products and has delivered 100+ websites, MVPs and platforms for founders in the UK, USA and UAE.
content:
An MVP development agency is a team that designs, builds and launches the first working version of a startup's product. The best agencies for early-stage founders work to a fixed scope and timeline, ship a product real customers can pay for, and hand over full ownership of the code. With a tightly scoped first release, a senior agency can launch a revenue-ready MVP in about 21 days.

:::takeaways
### Key Takeaways
- **An MVP tests whether customers will pay,** not whether you can build every feature. Scope it around one core workflow.
- **Time is the hidden cost.** A build that drags on for months burns runway and delays the feedback you need.
- **Compare agencies on outcomes, not hourly rates:** fixed scope, a delivery date, code ownership and post-launch support.
- **Ask five questions before you sign** to avoid the most common agency problems.
:::

## What Does an MVP Development Agency Do?

**An MVP agency turns a validated problem into a working product customers can use and pay for.** A complete engagement typically covers:

1. **Product scoping:** defining the core workflow, user roles and acceptance criteria.
2. **UX and UI design:** wireframes and a clean interface for the core journey.
3. **Engineering:** front end, back end, database, authentication and payments.
4. **Launch:** deployment, analytics, monitoring and basic SEO.
5. **Handover:** source code, documentation and access to every account.

## Why Do Many Agencies Take Months to Ship an MVP?

**Most delays come from process and scope, not from engineering difficulty.** Common causes include long discovery phases billed by the hour, features added mid-build without changing the timeline, junior developers learning on the project, and no single person accountable for shipping.

A fixed-scope, fixed-timeline model reverses those incentives: the agency is rewarded for delivering the agreed product on time rather than for hours spent.

## Should You Hire an Agency, a Freelancer or an In-House Team?

**Choose based on your stage, your technical skills and how much risk you can absorb.**

| Option | Best For | Main Risk |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **MVP agency** | Non-technical or busy founders who need a complete product fast | Choosing an agency without senior engineers or clear scope |
| **Freelancer** | Small, well-defined tasks or founders who can manage technical work | Single point of failure; gaps in design, QA or architecture |
| **In-house team** | Funded startups with proven demand and a long roadmap | Months of hiring before building; high fixed cost |
| **Technical co-founder** | Long-term company building with shared equity | Hard to find; equity dilution; can take a long time to match |

Many startups use an agency for the MVP, then hire in-house engineers once the product has traction. Clean code and documentation make that handover simple.

## How Does a 21-Day MVP Development Process Work?

**A 21-day MVP is three one-week sprints, each ending with something you can see and test.**

:::steps
### Days 1–5: Scope and Design
Agree the core workflow, user roles and acceptance criteria in writing. Design the key screens and the data model. Set up repositories, hosting and environments.
---
### Days 6–15: Build the Core Product
Engineer the main workflow end to end, including authentication, database, payments and any essential integration. Share progress builds with the founder for feedback.
---
### Days 16–21: Test, Launch and Hand Over
Test on real devices, fix issues, add analytics and monitoring, deploy to production and hand over the code, documentation and accounts.
:::

:::tip
### Bring three things to your first call
A one-sentence description of the customer and their problem, the single workflow a paying customer must complete, and any product, competitor or no-code prototype that shows what you mean. Those three inputs shorten scoping dramatically.
:::

For help deciding what goes in version one, read our [MVP scoping framework](/blog/startup-mvp-scoping-and-bubble-to-nextjs-migration). Building an AI product? Use the [AI SaaS MVP blueprint](/blog/how-to-build-ai-saas-mvp-in-21-days).

## What Should You Ask Before Signing With an MVP Agency?

**These five questions reveal most of what you need to know about an agency:**

:::grid
### Who will actually build my product?
Ask for the names and experience of the engineers on your project, not just the sales team. Senior engineers ship faster and make fewer architecture mistakes.
---
### What exactly is in scope, and what happens if it changes?
Get a written scope with acceptance criteria. Changes should become new milestones, not silent timeline extensions.
---
### Do I own 100% of the code and accounts?
Your company should own the source code, design files, database and every hosting and third-party account.
---
### What happens after launch?
Ask about bug fixes, support windows and how future feature sprints are planned and priced.
---
### Can I speak to a past client?
Real case studies and founder references are the strongest evidence that an agency delivers what it promises.
:::

:::casestudy

## Frequently Asked Questions

:::faq
### How long does it take an agency to build an MVP?
With a tightly scoped first release focused on one core workflow, a senior agency can build and launch an MVP in about 21 to 28 days. Broader scopes, many integrations or native mobile apps take longer.
### Is it better to hire an MVP agency or a freelancer?
An agency is usually better when you need design, engineering, testing and launch handled together with one accountable team. A freelancer can work well for small, clearly defined tasks if you can manage the technical work yourself.
### What should be included in an MVP?
Include only what a customer needs to complete the core job and pay for it: sign-up, the main workflow, payments if you charge from day one, and basic analytics. Leave secondary features for later versions.
### Will I own the code if an agency builds my MVP?
You should. Confirm in the contract that full ownership of the source code, design files, data and all accounts transfers to your company.
### Can an MVP agency build with both no-code and custom code?

title: What Belongs in a Startup MVP (and When to Migrate From Bubble.io to Next.js)
metaTitle: MVP Scoping Framework & Bubble.io to Next.js Migration
metaDescription: Decide what goes in your MVP with a must-have vs later framework, spot the signs you have outgrown Bubble.io, and migrate to Next.js without downtime.
excerpt: A practical framework for cutting your MVP to what customers will pay for, five signs a Bubble.io app has outgrown no-code, and a step-by-step plan to migrate to React and Next.js without downtime.
tags: what to include in an mvp
bubble io to custom code migration
altText: MVP feature prioritisation board next to a Bubble.io to Next.js migration plan
author: Muhammad Ahmad
authorBio: Muhammad Ahmad is the founder of WebMavien, a web and SaaS development agency. He has 8+ years of experience building React, Next.js and Bubble.io products and has delivered 100+ websites, MVPs and platforms for founders in the UK, USA and UAE.
content:
A startup MVP should include only the features a customer needs to complete one core job and pay for it: sign-up, the core workflow, payments if you charge from day one, and basic analytics. Everything else belongs in a later version. Once a no-code MVP proves demand, migrate to custom code such as React and Next.js when performance, SEO, platform costs or investor due diligence start limiting growth.

:::takeaways
### Key Takeaways
- **Scope around one paying workflow.** If a feature does not help a customer complete that workflow, it waits.
- **Use a simple must-have / later framework** and write acceptance criteria for every must-have.
- **No-code is a valid first stage,** not a failure. Migrate when specific triggers appear, not because of fashion.
- **Migrate gradually** using the strangler pattern so customers never experience downtime.
:::

## What Features Actually Belong in a Day-One MVP?

**A feature belongs in your MVP only if a customer cannot get the core value without it.** Use this framework to sort your feature list:

| Category | Include in V1? | Examples |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Must-have** | Yes | Sign-up and login, the core workflow, payments (if charging), essential notifications |
| **Should-have** | Only if cheap | Simple admin view, CSV export, basic search |
| **Could-have** | No, add after feedback | Advanced dashboards, team roles beyond two levels, integrations beyond the first |
| **Won't-have (yet)** | No | Native mobile apps, white-labelling, multi-language, AI features that are not the core value |

This is a version of the MoSCoW method (must, should, could, won't), adapted for early-stage products.

:::warning
### The three most common scope traps
**Building for imagined users** (features no real customer has asked for), **perfecting admin tools** before any customer exists, and **adding integrations "because enterprise buyers will want them"** before you have an enterprise buyer.
:::

## How Do You Prevent Scope Creep During an MVP Build?

**Write the scope down, attach acceptance criteria and treat every new idea as a future milestone.**

1. List each must-have feature with a one-line acceptance criterion ("A user can invite a teammate by email and the teammate can sign in").
2. Keep a separate "after launch" list and add every new idea to it, instead of to the current sprint.
3. Review the list with real users after launch and promote only features that customers request repeatedly.

## When Should You Migrate From Bubble.io to Next.js?

**Migrate when the platform, not your team, becomes the limit on growth.** These five triggers are the clearest signals:

:::grid
### Performance Problems
Pages or workflows become slow as data grows, and optimisation inside the platform no longer helps.
---
### Rising Platform Usage Costs
Bubble.io bills by workload units. As usage grows, platform costs can rise faster than revenue for data-heavy apps.
---
### SEO Becomes a Growth Channel
Content and landing pages that need strong Core Web Vitals and fine control over rendering are easier to build in Next.js.
---
### Complex Logic or Integrations
Heavy data processing, real-time features, complex permissions or many integrations become hard to maintain visually.
---
### Investor Technical Due Diligence
Some investors and acquirers prefer a codebase they can audit, test and hand to an engineering team.
:::

If none of these apply, staying on Bubble.io is often the right decision. Our [React / Next.js vs Bubble.io comparison](/blog/react-vs-bubble-io-for-saas-mvp-2026) explains the trade-offs in detail.

## How Do You Migrate From Bubble.io to Next.js Without Downtime?

**Use the strangler pattern: replace the product piece by piece while the old app keeps running, then switch traffic over in stages.**

:::steps
### Audit and Map the Existing App
Document every data type, workflow, API connector, privacy rule and plugin in the Bubble app. This becomes the migration checklist.
---
### Design the New Data Model and Export Data
Design a relational schema (usually PostgreSQL) and write scripts to export and transform Bubble data through its Data API, including user accounts and file references.
---
### Rebuild Public Pages First
Move marketing and SEO pages to Next.js first. They carry little risk and deliver immediate performance and search benefits.
---
### Rebuild Core Workflows Behind the Scenes
Build and test the application features in Next.js against a copy of production data while customers continue to use Bubble.
---
### Cut Over and Keep a Rollback Plan
Run a final data sync, switch traffic to the new app, keep the Bubble app read-only for a short period as a fallback, and monitor errors closely.
:::

:::tip
### Plan password resets in advance
User passwords usually cannot be exported from no-code platforms. Plan a smooth "set your new password" email flow or magic-link sign-in so the cutover does not feel like a forced reset.
:::

:::casestudy

:::faq
### What is the minimum feature set for an MVP?
The minimum feature set is whatever a customer needs to complete one core job and pay for it, usually sign-up, the main workflow, payments if you charge from day one, and basic analytics.
### How do I decide which features to cut from my MVP?
Ask whether a customer can still get the core value without the feature. If they can, move it to a later version. A must, should, could and won't (MoSCoW) list makes the decision explicit.
### Is Bubble.io good enough for an MVP?
Yes, for many products. Bubble.io is fast for validating workflows, internal tools and marketplaces. It becomes limiting when performance, SEO, platform costs or complex logic start to restrict growth.
### How long does a Bubble.io to Next.js migration take?
It depends on the number of workflows, data types and integrations. Smaller apps can be migrated in a few weeks; larger ones are migrated in phases using the strangler pattern so customers are not affected.
### Will I lose my data when migrating from Bubble.io?
No, if the migration is planned properly. Data is exported through Bubble's Data API, transformed into the new schema, tested against a copy of production and synced again just before cutover.

title: Custom CRM Development vs HubSpot & Salesforce: A Total Cost of Ownership Comparison
metaTitle: Custom CRM vs HubSpot & Salesforce: Cost of Ownership Guide
metaDescription: Custom CRM or HubSpot and Salesforce? Compare per-seat licences, add-ons, customisation, data ownership and 3-year cost of ownership to find break-even.
excerpt: When does building a custom CRM cost less than paying for HubSpot or Salesforce? A clear framework for comparing three-year cost of ownership, plus the operational signs it is time to switch and how to migrate safely.
altText: Comparison chart of custom CRM ownership costs against HubSpot and Salesforce licences over three years
author: Muhammad Ahmad
authorBio: Muhammad Ahmad is the founder of WebMavien, a web and SaaS development agency. He has 8+ years of experience building React, Next.js and Bubble.io products and has delivered 100+ websites, MVPs and platforms for founders in the UK, USA and UAE.
content:
A custom CRM usually costs more upfront than HubSpot or Salesforce but less over time once a team has many users, pays for several add-on tools, or runs workflows that off-the-shelf CRMs cannot model. The decision comes down to three-year total cost of ownership: licences, add-ons, admin and consultant time on one side, and build cost, hosting and maintenance on the other.

:::takeaways
### Key Takeaways
- **Off-the-shelf CRMs are the right choice for small teams** with standard sales pipelines and fewer than about ten users.
- **Per-seat pricing is the main cost multiplier.** Every new salesperson, support agent or partner login adds a recurring licence.
- **Custom CRMs remove seat fees and tool sprawl,** and fit workflows such as bookings, fulfilment and client portals that standard CRMs handle poorly.
- **Compare over three years, not one,** and include add-ons, admin time and price increases at renewal.
:::

## Is a Custom CRM Cheaper Than HubSpot or Salesforce?

**For small teams with standard sales processes, no. For growing, operations-heavy teams, often yes.** The break-even point depends on how many users you have, how many extra tools you pay for alongside your CRM, and how much custom work you already pay consultants to do.

| Cost Factor | HubSpot / Salesforce | Custom CRM |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Upfront cost** | Low; onboarding packages for higher tiers | Higher; one-time design and build |
| **Recurring licences** | Per seat, per month, rising with team size and tier | No per-seat fees |
| **Add-on tools** | Often needed for scheduling, portals, forms, chat or automation | Built in to match your workflow |
| **Customisation** | Limited by platform objects; complex changes need admins or consultants | Built around your exact data and process |
| **Price increases** | Set by the vendor at renewal | Hosting costs only; you control the roadmap |
| **Data ownership** | Data lives on the vendor's platform | Your database, your code, your infrastructure |
| **Time to start** | Same day | Typically 3–6 weeks for a focused first version |

:::tip
### How to run your own three-year comparison
Add up today's monthly CRM licences, every add-on tool (scheduling, forms, chat, portals, automation) and any admin or consultant fees. Multiply by 36, then add expected new hires and tier upgrades. Compare that total with a quote for a custom build plus three years of hosting and support.
:::

## What Problems Make Companies Build Their Own CRM?

**Companies rarely build a CRM to save money alone.** They build one because their business no longer fits a standard "contacts and deals" model.

:::grid
### Too Many Disconnected Tools
The CRM, scheduling tool, live chat, form builder and automation platform each hold part of the customer record, and staff switch between tabs all day.
---
### Workflows That Do Not Fit
Bookings, field service, multi-party marketplaces, recruitment pipelines or project delivery have to be forced into deal stages with workarounds.
---
### No Proper Client Portal
Customers and partners need a branded login to upload documents, book slots and track progress, which standard CRMs do not offer natively.
:::

For a full checklist, read [7 signs your business has outgrown spreadsheets and off-the-shelf CRMs](/blog/when-to-build-custom-crm-workflows-automation).

## When Should You Stay With HubSpot or Salesforce?

**Stay with an off-the-shelf CRM if your process is standard and your team is small.** HubSpot and Salesforce are excellent products with large ecosystems. They are the better choice when:

- You have a small team running a conventional B2B sales or email marketing funnel.
- You rely heavily on built-in marketing automation, ad integrations or app marketplaces.
- You do not need an external client portal or custom operational workflows.
- You have no budget or appetite to own and maintain software.

A middle path is also common: keep HubSpot or Salesforce for marketing and build a custom operations portal that syncs with it through their APIs.

## How Do You Move From HubSpot or Salesforce Without Disruption?

**Run the new CRM alongside the old one, migrate data in stages and cancel licences only after the team has switched.**

:::steps
### Map the Workflows Your Team Actually Uses
List the screens, fields, automations and reports people use every week. Drop anything unused rather than rebuilding it.
---
### Build the Core Pipeline and Portal First
Launch the essential records, pipeline stages, permissions, calendar sync and notifications as the first release.
---
### Export, Clean and Import Your Data
Export contacts, companies, deals, notes and activity history through the vendor's export tools or API, clean duplicates, and import into your own database.
---
### Train the Team and Switch Off Licences
Because the interface uses your company's own terms and process, training is short. Cancel seats once usage moves over, ideally timed to your renewal date.
:::

## Frequently Asked Questions

:::faq
### Is it worth building a custom CRM?
It is worth it when per-seat licences and add-on tools are growing quickly, or when your workflows (bookings, fulfilment, client portals, marketplaces) do not fit a standard CRM. Small teams with conventional sales processes are usually better served by HubSpot or Salesforce.
### How long does it take to build a custom CRM?
A focused first version covering contacts, pipeline, permissions, notifications and key integrations typically takes about 3 to 6 weeks. More complex portals and automations can be added in later sprints.
### Can a custom CRM integrate with Gmail, Outlook, Slack and accounting software?
Yes. Custom CRMs commonly integrate with Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Slack, Stripe, WhatsApp and accounting tools such as QuickBooks or Xero through their APIs and webhooks.
### Can I migrate my data out of HubSpot or Salesforce?
Yes. Both platforms provide data export tools and APIs, so contacts, companies, deals and activity history can be exported, cleaned and imported into a custom CRM.
### Who owns a custom CRM after it is built?
Your company should own the source code, database and infrastructure. Confirm full IP transfer in your development contract.

title: 7 Signs Your Business Has Outgrown Spreadsheets and Off-the-Shelf CRMs
metaTitle: 7 Signs You Need a Custom CRM & Workflow Automation
metaDescription: Running sales and operations on spreadsheets or a CRM you have outgrown? Seven clear signs you need a custom CRM, and the modules worth building first.

author: Muhammad Ahmad
authorBio: Muhammad Ahmad is the founder of WebMavien, a web and SaaS development agency. He has 8+ years of experience building React, Next.js and Bubble.io products and has delivered 100+ websites, MVPs and platforms for founders in the UK, USA and UAE.
content:
You need a custom CRM when your team re-enters the same data in several tools, your process does not fit standard CRM stages, customers have no self-service portal, managers cannot get reliable reports without manual work, and per-seat licences keep rising. A custom CRM brings customer records, operational workflows and automation into one system built around how your business actually works.

:::takeaways
### Key Takeaways
- **Manual re-entry is the clearest signal.** If staff copy the same information between spreadsheets, email, chat and accounting tools, you are paying for it in hours and errors.
- **Custom CRMs fit your process, not the other way around.** Bookings, fulfilment, field work and partner management can be modelled directly.
- **Start with the highest-value modules:** a unified customer record, workflow automation, a client portal and reporting.
- **Compliance depends on market.** UK GDPR, US state privacy laws and the UAE PDPL all affect how CRM data must be handled.
:::

## What Are the 7 Signs Your Company Needs a Custom CRM?

**If three or more of these apply, a custom CRM is worth evaluating.**

:::steps
### Your Team Re-Enters the Same Data in Several Places
Lead details are typed into a spreadsheet, then the CRM, then an invoice, then a project tool. Every copy creates delay and mistakes.
---
### Your Real Process Does Not Fit "Contacts and Deals"
Bookings, onboarding steps, inspections, multi-party transactions or renewals are tracked in side spreadsheets because the CRM cannot model them.
---
### Customer Conversations Live in Personal Inboxes and WhatsApp
When a staff member is away or leaves, the history goes with them.
---
### Managers Build Reports by Hand
Weekly numbers come from exporting several tools into a spreadsheet, so reports are late and disputed.
---
### Customers Keep Asking "What Is the Status?"
There is no portal where clients can upload documents, approve work or track progress, so your team answers the same questions by phone and email.
---
### Your Software Bill Grows With Every Hire
Per-seat licences for the CRM plus separate scheduling, forms, chat and automation tools rise every time the team grows.
---
### Automations Are Fragile
Zaps and scripts connecting tools break silently, and nobody is sure which system holds the correct data.
:::

## What Can a Custom CRM Automate?

**The best candidates for automation are repetitive, rule-based tasks that currently depend on someone remembering to do them.** Typical examples include:

- Assigning new leads to the right person based on location, product or source.
- Sending follow-up reminders and booking confirmations automatically.
- Creating invoices in your accounting software when a deal is won.
- Requesting reviews after a job is completed.
- Alerting managers when a deal or ticket stalls for too long.
- Scoring leads using rules or AI based on fit and engagement.

## Which Custom CRM Modules Deliver the Most Value First?

**Build the modules that remove the most manual work, then expand.** Four modules usually come first:

:::grid
### Unified Customer Record
One profile for each customer that combines contact details, conversations, deals, bookings, documents and payments.
---
### Pipeline and Workflow Engine
Stages, tasks and automations that match your actual process, from enquiry to delivery and renewal.
---
### Client or Partner Portal
A secure, branded login where customers and partners upload files, book slots, approve work and track progress.
---
### Reporting Dashboard
Live metrics for pipeline, revenue, response times and team performance, without manual exports.
:::

If cost is the main question, compare your current spend using our [custom CRM vs HubSpot and Salesforce cost guide](/blog/custom-crm-development-vs-hubspot-salesforce-cost).

## How Does CRM Data Compliance Work in the UK, USA and UAE?

**A CRM holds personal data, so it must follow the privacy laws of the markets you serve.** Build these requirements in from the start:

| Market | Key Rules | What Your CRM Needs |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **United Kingdom** | UK GDPR, Data Protection Act 2018, PECR for electronic marketing | Lawful basis records, marketing consent tracking, data subject access and deletion tools |
| **United States** | State privacy laws such as CCPA/CPRA; HIPAA for health data; CAN-SPAM for email | Opt-out handling, data access and deletion requests, access controls and audit logs |
| **UAE** | Federal PDPL onshore; DIFC and ADGM data protection laws in those free zones | Consent records, data minimisation, secure storage and cross-border transfer controls |

Role-based permissions, audit logs, encryption and clear data retention rules help with all three. Our regional guides cover the [UK](/blog/web-development-mvp-ecommerce-agency-uk-2026), [USA](/blog/saas-mvp-custom-crm-agency-usa-2026) and [UAE](/blog/web-ecommerce-crm-development-agency-dubai-uae-2026) in more depth.

### When should a business stop using spreadsheets as a CRM?
When several people need to update the same records, data is copied between tools, customers ask for status updates you cannot answer quickly, or reporting requires manual exports. At that point a CRM saves time and reduces errors.
### What is the difference between a CRM and a custom CRM?
An off-the-shelf CRM such as HubSpot or Salesforce provides a standard data model and features for many businesses. A custom CRM is built around one company's specific process, data and integrations, with no per-seat licence fees.

Yes. A client portal is one of the most common reasons companies build a custom CRM. Customers can log in to upload documents, book appointments, approve work and track progress.

title: Shopify vs Custom Next.js E-Commerce in 2026: Which Is Right for Your Brand?
metaTitle: Shopify vs Custom Next.js E-Commerce (2026 Comparison)
metaDescription: Shopify or a custom Next.js store? Compare launch speed, app costs, performance, SEO control, checkout flexibility and the headless middle path.
excerpt: An honest comparison of Shopify themes, headless Shopify and fully custom Next.js stores: when Shopify is the right call, when brands outgrow it, and how to choose the right architecture for your stage.
altText: Comparison of a Shopify theme storefront and a custom Next.js e-commerce storefront on mobile
author: Muhammad Ahmad
authorBio: Muhammad Ahmad is the founder of WebMavien, a web and SaaS development agency. He has 8+ years of experience building React, Next.js and Bubble.io products and has delivered 100+ websites, MVPs and platforms for founders in the UK, USA and UAE.
content:
Shopify is the right choice for most new and small online stores because it is fast to launch and handles payments, hosting and security for you. A custom Next.js storefront becomes the better choice when app fees and theme limits slow you down, performance and SEO need fine control, or your products, pricing or checkout need logic Shopify cannot support. Headless Shopify, a Next.js front end on Shopify's back end, is a popular middle path.

:::takeaways
### Key Takeaways
- **Start on Shopify** if you are testing products, have a small catalogue and need to sell this week.
- **Watch for the warning signs:** a growing stack of paid apps, slow mobile pages, theme workarounds and checkout limitations.
- **Headless Shopify** keeps Shopify's catalogue, checkout and admin while giving you a fast, fully custom Next.js front end.
- **Fully custom** makes sense for complex B2B pricing, subscriptions, configurators, marketplaces or brands that want full ownership.
:::

## How Do Shopify, Headless Shopify and Custom Next.js Compare?

**They sit on a spectrum from fastest to launch to most control.**

| Factor | Shopify Theme | Headless Shopify + Next.js | Fully Custom Next.js |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Time to launch** | Days | Weeks | Weeks |
| **Upfront effort** | Lowest | Medium | Highest |
| **Recurring costs** | Plan fees, app subscriptions, transaction fees if not using Shopify Payments | Plan fees plus hosting; fewer apps | Hosting and payment processing |
| **Page speed control** | Limited by theme and app scripts | Full front-end control | Full control |
| **SEO control** | Good basics; fixed URL structures | Full control over URLs, rendering and structured data | Full control |
| **Checkout customisation** | Limited, more on Shopify Plus | Shopify checkout | Fully custom with Stripe or other providers |
| **Complex products and pricing** | Needs apps and workarounds | Partly; depends on back end | Unlimited |
| **Ownership** | Platform-dependent | Front end owned; back end on Shopify | Full ownership |

## When Should an E-Commerce Brand Move Beyond a Shopify Theme?

**Move when Shopify's limits start costing you more in fees, speed or lost sales than a custom build would.** Common signs include:

:::grid
### App Stack Keeps Growing
Reviews, bundles, subscriptions, upsells, filters and loyalty each need a paid app, and each adds scripts that slow down pages.
---
### Slow Mobile Performance
Core Web Vitals fail on mobile because of theme code and third-party scripts, hurting both conversion and search rankings.
---
### Theme Workarounds Everywhere
Developers spend more time fighting the theme than building features customers want.
---
### Business Logic Shopify Cannot Model
B2B price lists, quote requests, product configurators, rentals or multi-vendor catalogues need custom logic.
:::

:::tip
### Measure before you migrate
Check your Core Web Vitals in Google Search Console and PageSpeed Insights, list every paid app and what it does, and calculate how much revenue mobile visitors generate. That data tells you whether a rebuild will pay off.
:::

## What Is Headless Shopify (and When Is It the Best Option)?

**Headless Shopify uses Shopify as the back end for products, inventory, orders and checkout, while a separate front end, usually built in Next.js, renders the storefront.** The two connect through Shopify's Storefront API.

It is the best option when your team likes Shopify's admin and checkout but needs a faster, more distinctive storefront and full SEO control. It is less suitable when the main problem is business logic Shopify's back end cannot handle; in that case a fully custom store is usually the better fit.

## Is a Custom Next.js Store Better for SEO?

**A custom Next.js store gives you more SEO control, and control is what helps rankings once the basics are covered.** With Next.js you can choose server-side or static rendering per page, design clean URL structures, add complete Product and Breadcrumb structured data, optimise images automatically and keep third-party scripts to a minimum. Shopify handles SEO basics well, but its URL patterns are fixed and app scripts often hurt page speed.

For the specific fixes that improve rankings and conversion on any platform, see our [e-commerce SEO and checkout optimisation checklist](/blog/ecommerce-seo-and-checkout-conversion-optimization).

:::casestudy
