## Frequently Asked Questions

:::faq
### Is Shopify or a custom website better for e-commerce?
Shopify is better for launching quickly with a small catalogue and standard products. A custom website is better when you need faster performance, full SEO control, complex pricing or product logic, or freedom from app and platform fees.
### What is headless Shopify?
Headless Shopify means using Shopify for products, inventory, orders and checkout while building the storefront separately, typically in Next.js, and connecting the two through Shopify's Storefront API.
### Is Next.js good for e-commerce?
Yes. Next.js supports fast server-rendered and static pages, image optimisation and full control over metadata and structured data, which helps both conversion rates and search rankings.
### Can I move from Shopify to a custom store without losing SEO?
Yes, if you keep or redirect every product, collection and content URL with 301 redirects, carry over titles, descriptions and structured data, and monitor Search Console closely after launch.
### How long does it take to build a custom e-commerce store?
A focused custom or headless storefront can typically be launched in about 3 to 6 weeks, depending on catalogue size, integrations and checkout requirements.

title: From Instagram and WhatsApp DMs to an Automated Online Store: A Step-by-Step Guide
metaTitle: Move From Instagram & WhatsApp DM Orders to an Online Store
metaDescription: Still taking orders in Instagram and WhatsApp DMs? Learn what manual ordering costs you and how to move customers to an automated online store in four weeks.
excerpt: Selling through Instagram and WhatsApp DMs works for your first orders, then becomes your biggest bottleneck. Here is what it costs in lost sales and time, and a four-week plan to move to automated checkout.

content:
If you take orders through Instagram or WhatsApp direct messages, you lose sales whenever you are slow to reply, spend hours confirming details and payments by hand, and cannot see which products and campaigns actually sell. An online store with automated checkout lets customers buy instantly from your social links, takes payment on the spot and sends orders straight to fulfilment, while your social accounts keep doing what they do best: attracting buyers.

:::takeaways
### Key Takeaways
- **DM selling does not scale.** Every order needs a conversation, so sales are capped by how fast you can reply.
- **Impulse buyers do not wait.** Shoppers who see a post late at night often move on if nobody answers.
- **An automated store keeps social selling,** but sends buyers to a fast checkout with wallets like Apple Pay and Google Pay.
- **The switch can be done in about four weeks** with a focused build and a clear launch plan for your followers.
:::

## What Does Selling Through DMs Really Cost You?

**The biggest cost is not visible: it is the sales you never see.** Manual ordering creates four kinds of loss:

:::grid
### Missed Impulse Purchases
A shopper asks for the price at midnight, gets a reply the next morning and has already lost interest.
---
### Hours of Admin
Every order means confirming size, stock, address and payment by hand, then copying details to a delivery service.
---
### Payment and Order Errors
Screenshots of bank transfers, wrong addresses and forgotten orders lead to refunds and unhappy customers.
---
### No Data to Grow With
You cannot easily see which products, posts or customers drive revenue, so marketing decisions are guesswork.
:::

## Should You Use a Marketplace, Shopify or a Custom Store?

**Choose based on how many products you sell, how unique your brand experience needs to be, and how fast you want to grow.**

| Option | Good For | Limitations |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Instagram or WhatsApp catalogue only** | Very early testing | Still relies on chat; limited checkout and data |
| **Shopify or similar platform** | Quick launch with standard products | App fees and theme limits as you grow |
| **Custom store (React or Next.js)** | Brands with strong storytelling, custom bundles or growth plans | Higher upfront effort; needs a good development partner |

For a full comparison, read [Shopify vs custom Next.js e-commerce](/blog/shopify-vs-custom-nextjs-ecommerce-2026).

## What Affects the Cost of an Automated Online Store?

**Cost depends on scope, not on the platform name.** The main factors are:

- **Catalogue size and variants:** a few products with sizes is simpler than hundreds with complex options.
- **Payment methods:** cards, Apple Pay, Google Pay, buy-now-pay-later and cash on delivery each add setup work.
- **Delivery integrations:** connecting to courier services for rates and labels.
- **Messaging automation:** order confirmations and updates by email, SMS or WhatsApp.
- **Content and design:** product photography, brand storytelling pages and custom design.
- **Admin needs:** stock management, discount codes and sales reports.

A focused first version with your best-selling products, wallet payments and automated notifications keeps the scope tight and the launch fast.

## How Do You Move Customers From DMs to Automated Checkout?

**Follow a four-week plan, then train your audience to use the new link.**

:::steps
### Week 1: Products, Brand and Payments
Choose the products to launch with, gather photos and descriptions, and set up payments, including wallet options such as Apple Pay and Google Pay.
---
### Week 2: Build the Store
Build product pages, cart and checkout, delivery options and order confirmation emails or messages, designed mobile-first because most social traffic is mobile.
---
### Week 3: Automate Fulfilment
Connect orders to your delivery process, set up stock tracking, and add automatic order updates so customers stop messaging to ask where their parcel is.
---
### Week 4: Launch to Your Followers
Add the store link to your bio, use product tags and stories, and reply to DM enquiries with a direct product link. Offer a small first-order incentive to change buying habits.
:::

A focused store with your main products, wallet payments and automated notifications can typically be launched in about four weeks.

Yes, when the site loads quickly, shows clear product information, delivery and returns policies, and offers familiar payment methods such as Apple Pay, Google Pay and major cards.

title: E-Commerce SEO and Checkout Optimisation: 7 Engineering Fixes That Reduce Cart Abandonment
metaTitle: E-Commerce SEO & Checkout Optimisation: 7 Engineering Fixes
metaDescription: Seven engineering fixes that cut cart abandonment and lift organic traffic: Core Web Vitals, wallet and guest checkout, product schema and more.
excerpt: Around seven in ten online shopping carts are abandoned. These seven technical fixes, from Core Web Vitals and express wallet checkout to Product structured data, improve both conversion rate and search visibility.
altText: Mobile checkout screen with express wallet payment buttons and a fast-loading product page
author: Muhammad Ahmad
authorBio: Muhammad Ahmad is the founder of WebMavien, a web and SaaS development agency. He has 8+ years of experience building React, Next.js and Bubble.io products and has delivered 100+ websites, MVPs and platforms for founders in the UK, USA and UAE.
content:
Cart abandonment averages around 70% according to Baymard Institute's research. Much of it is caused by fixable technical issues: slow pages, forced account creation, long forms, unexpected costs revealed late and too few payment options. The same engineering work that fixes checkout (fast pages, clean structure and accurate product data) also improves e-commerce SEO.

:::takeaways
### Key Takeaways
- **Speed is both a ranking and a conversion factor.** Aim for good Core Web Vitals on mobile: LCP within 2.5 seconds, INP under 200 milliseconds and CLS below 0.1.
- **Express wallets and guest checkout** remove the biggest sources of checkout friction.
- **Show total costs early.** Unexpected delivery fees and taxes at the last step are a leading cause of abandonment.
- **Structured data and crawlable navigation** help products appear in search results with prices, availability and reviews.
:::

## Why Do Shoppers Abandon Their Carts?

**Most abandonment comes from friction and surprise rather than from a change of mind.** Baymard Institute's checkout research consistently finds that the leading reasons include extra costs being too high, being required to create an account, a long or complicated checkout, not seeing the total cost up front, and not trusting the site with card details. Every one of these can be reduced with better engineering and design.

## What Are the 7 Engineering Fixes That Recover Lost Revenue?

:::steps
### Pass Core Web Vitals on Mobile
Optimise the Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) image, serve modern image formats, render product pages on the server or statically, and remove unused third-party scripts. Google's thresholds for a good experience are LCP within 2.5 seconds, INP under 200 milliseconds and CLS below 0.1.
---
### Offer Express Wallet Checkout
Show Apple Pay, Google Pay and other wallet buttons on product pages and in the cart, not only at the last step. Wallets fill in payment and address details in one tap.
---
### Allow Guest Checkout
Let customers buy without creating an account, and offer to save their details after the order is complete.
---
### Show Total Costs Early
Display delivery costs, taxes and delivery dates on product and cart pages, or offer a delivery calculator, so there are no surprises at payment.
---
### Shorten and Simplify Forms
Use address autocomplete, the correct mobile keyboard for each field, inline validation and the fewest possible fields.
---
### Add Product and Breadcrumb Structured Data
Mark up product pages with schema.org Product data, including price, availability, reviews and shipping details where available, so search engines can show rich results.
---
### Make Category Navigation Crawlable
Ensure category and filter pages have clean URLs, internal links and canonical tags, and prevent endless filter combinations from creating thousands of duplicate pages.
:::

:::tip
### Use a slide-over cart
A cart that opens as a side panel keeps shoppers on the product page, shows the running total and offers express checkout, without forcing a full page load.
:::

## How Does Technical SEO Differ for Online Stores?

**E-commerce sites face SEO problems that content sites do not: thousands of near-identical pages, out-of-stock products and faceted navigation.** Focus on these areas:

| Area | What to Do |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Faceted navigation** | Index only valuable filter combinations; use canonical tags and avoid crawl traps |
| **Out-of-stock products** | Keep pages live with availability updated if the product returns; redirect permanently discontinued items to the closest alternative |
| **Product descriptions** | Write unique descriptions instead of copying manufacturer text |
| **Category pages** | Add short, useful introductory copy and FAQs to target broader search terms |
| **Images** | Descriptive file names and alt text, modern formats and responsive sizes |
| **Internal linking** | Link related products, categories and buying guides |

Your platform choice affects how much of this you control. See [Shopify vs custom Next.js e-commerce](/blog/shopify-vs-custom-nextjs-ecommerce-2026) for the trade-offs.

## How Do You Measure Whether the Fixes Worked?

**Track a small set of metrics before and after each change.** Use field data for Core Web Vitals from Google Search Console, checkout funnel steps in your analytics tool (cart, checkout start, payment, purchase), conversion rate by device, organic clicks and impressions for product and category pages, and rich result eligibility in Search Console.

:::casestudy

:::faq
### What is the average cart abandonment rate?
Baymard Institute's aggregate of published studies puts the average online shopping cart abandonment rate at around 70%.
### Do Core Web Vitals affect e-commerce rankings?
Yes. Core Web Vitals are part of Google's page experience signals. Good scores also improve user experience, which tends to raise conversion rates, especially on mobile.
### Does adding Apple Pay and Google Pay increase conversions?
Express wallets typically reduce checkout friction because they fill in payment and shipping details in one step. They are especially effective on mobile, where typing card and address details is slow.
### What structured data should an online store use?
Use schema.org Product markup with offers, price, availability and reviews on product pages, BreadcrumbList for navigation, and Organization data for the brand. Validate it with Google's Rich Results Test.
### Should online stores allow guest checkout?
Yes. Being forced to create an account is one of the most common reasons shoppers abandon checkout. Offer account creation after purchase instead.
:::

title: How to Build a Two-Sided Marketplace in 2026: Architecture, Payments and Launch Guide
metaTitle: How to Build a Two-Sided Marketplace: 2026 Guide
metaDescription: How to build a two-sided marketplace: core modules, Stripe Connect split payments, preventing platform leakage, Bubble.io vs Next.js, and regional rules.
excerpt: A practical blueprint for marketplace founders: the five modules every marketplace MVP needs, how split payments work with Stripe Connect, how to stop buyers and sellers going around you, and which stack to choose.
altText: Marketplace architecture diagram showing buyers, sellers, listings and split payments through Stripe Connect
author: Muhammad Ahmad
authorBio: Muhammad Ahmad is the founder of WebMavien, a web and SaaS development agency. He has 8+ years of experience building React, Next.js and Bubble.io products and has delivered 100+ websites, MVPs and platforms for founders in the UK, USA and UAE.
content:
To build a two-sided marketplace, launch with five core modules: user accounts for buyers and sellers, listings with search, booking or ordering, split payments through a provider such as Stripe Connect, and reviews and messaging. Start in one niche and one location, solve supply first, and design payments and trust features so both sides have a reason to stay on the platform.

:::takeaways
### Key Takeaways
- **Pick a narrow niche and seed supply first.** Buyers arrive when there is enough to choose from.
- **Five modules make a marketplace MVP:** accounts, listings and search, booking or ordering, split payments, and reviews and messaging.
- **Stripe Connect handles seller onboarding, identity checks and payouts,** so you do not hold other people's money yourself.
- **Platform leakage is the biggest business risk.** Give both sides real value for transacting on the platform.
:::

## What Is a Two-Sided Marketplace?

**A two-sided marketplace is a platform that connects two distinct groups, typically buyers and sellers or customers and service providers, and earns money by facilitating transactions between them.** Examples include rental, booking, freelance, B2B sourcing and local services platforms. The platform's value grows as more participants join each side, which is why the early launch strategy matters as much as the software.

## What Are the 5 Core Modules of a Marketplace MVP?

:::steps
### Accounts and Profiles for Both Sides
Separate onboarding flows for buyers and sellers, with verification steps for sellers and editable public profiles.
---
### Listings and Search
Listing creation with photos, pricing and availability, plus search and filters by location, category, date or price.
---
### Booking, Ordering or Requests
The core transaction flow: instant booking, request-to-book, quote requests or cart checkout depending on the model.
---
### Split Payments and Payouts
Collect payment from the buyer, keep the platform fee and pay the seller automatically, with refunds and disputes handled.
---
### Reviews, Messaging and Notifications
Two-way reviews, on-platform messaging and email or SMS notifications build trust and keep conversations inside the platform.
:::

Admin tools for moderating listings, resolving disputes and viewing transactions are also essential, but can start simple.

## How Do Split Payments and Escrow Work With Stripe Connect?

**Stripe Connect lets a platform accept payments from buyers, take a fee and route the rest to sellers' connected accounts, while Stripe handles seller identity verification and payouts.** Common patterns include:

| Payment Pattern | How It Works | Best For |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Destination charges** | The platform charges the buyer and transfers the seller's share to their connected account | Most simple marketplaces |
| **Separate charges and transfers** | The platform charges first and transfers funds later, possibly to several sellers | Multi-seller carts, delayed payouts, service completion |
| **Direct charges** | The seller's account charges the buyer and the platform takes an application fee | Platforms where sellers own the customer relationship |

To hold funds until a service is delivered, platforms commonly delay transfers or payouts until the job is confirmed. Check Stripe's documentation for availability in your countries and for limits on how long funds can be held.

:::tip
### Let the payment provider handle compliance
Holding and moving other people's money can bring licensing obligations. Using Stripe Connect's onboarding, verification and payouts keeps most of that burden with a regulated provider.
:::

## How Do You Prevent Platform Leakage?

**Platform leakage (also called disintermediation) happens when buyers and sellers meet on your marketplace, then transact directly to avoid fees.** The best defence is to make the platform more valuable than going around it:

- **Payment protection:** refunds, dispute resolution and secure payment for buyers; guaranteed payout for sellers.
- **Reputation:** reviews and ratings only count for transactions completed on the platform.
- **Tools sellers need:** calendars, invoicing, messaging and analytics that make their work easier.
- **Smart contact sharing:** reveal contact details only after booking is confirmed.
- **Fair fees:** a commission that reflects the value delivered, sometimes lower for repeat customers.

## Should You Build Your Marketplace on Bubble.io or Next.js?

**Bubble.io is a strong choice for validating a marketplace quickly; Next.js is better when SEO, performance and complex logic are central.** Marketplaces often depend on search traffic to listing pages, which favours Next.js long term. Read our full [React / Next.js vs Bubble.io comparison](/blog/react-vs-bubble-io-for-saas-mvp-2026) and the guide to [what drives development cost](/blog/saas-application-development-cost-2026).

## How Do Marketplace Requirements Differ in the USA, UK and UAE?

- **USA:** sales tax collection rules (including marketplace facilitator laws in many states), seller tax reporting and state privacy laws.
- **UK:** UK GDPR, consumer protection rules for online sales and HMRC rules that require digital platforms to report seller income.
- **UAE:** the federal PDPL or free zone data laws, VAT, and checking that your payment provider supports onshore payouts. See our [UAE guide](/blog/web-ecommerce-crm-development-agency-dubai-uae-2026).

:::casestudy

## Frequently Asked Questions

:::faq
### What features does a marketplace MVP need?
A marketplace MVP needs accounts and profiles for both sides, listings with search, a booking or ordering flow, split payments and payouts, and reviews and messaging, plus a simple admin panel for moderation.
### How do marketplaces handle payments between buyers and sellers?
Most use a payment platform such as Stripe Connect, which collects the buyer's payment, deducts the platform fee and pays the seller's connected account, while handling identity verification and payouts.
### How do you solve the chicken-and-egg problem in a marketplace?
Focus on one niche and location, recruit and onboard supply manually before launch, and make the first buyers' experience excellent. Supply usually needs to come first.
### How long does it take to build a marketplace MVP?
A focused marketplace MVP with the five core modules can typically be built in about 4 to 8 weeks, depending on payment complexity, search requirements and integrations.
### How do marketplaces stop users from transacting off-platform?
By offering protection, reputation and tools that only work on the platform, revealing contact details after booking, and keeping fees proportional to the value provided.
:::

title: How to Build and Launch an AI SaaS MVP in 21 Days (Founder Blueprint)
metaTitle: How to Build an AI SaaS MVP in 21 Days: Founder Blueprint
metaDescription: A week-by-week plan to build an AI SaaS MVP in 21 days: scoping, tech stack, RAG, Stripe billing, AI cost control and launch, from engineers who ship.
excerpt: A practical three-week plan for founders: what to build in each week, which tech stack to use, how to keep AI costs under control, and what to leave out of version one.
breadcrumbTitle: Build an AI SaaS MVP in 21 Days
tags: how to build an ai saas mvp
altText: Three-week AI SaaS MVP roadmap showing scoping, core build and launch milestones
author: Muhammad Ahmad
authorBio: Muhammad Ahmad is the founder of WebMavien, a web and SaaS development agency. He has 8+ years of experience building React, Next.js and Bubble.io products and has delivered 100+ websites, MVPs and platforms for founders in the UK, USA and UAE.
content:
You can build and launch an AI SaaS MVP in 21 days if you limit version one to a single core workflow, use managed services for authentication, payments and hosting, and follow a fixed three-week plan: week one for scope, data model and AI prototype; week two for the core product and billing; week three for hardening, onboarding and launch.

:::takeaways
### Key Takeaways
- **One workflow, done well.** A 21-day MVP automates one painful, repeated job for one type of customer. Everything else waits for version two.
- **Prototype the AI first.** Test prompts, retrieval and output quality on real sample data in week one, before building screens around them.
- **Use proven infrastructure.** Next.js, a managed Postgres database, Stripe and a hosted model API let a small team ship production-quality software fast.
- **Engineer for margins from day one.** Caching, smaller models for simple steps and per-plan usage limits keep AI costs predictable.
:::

## Why Build an AI SaaS MVP in Three Weeks?

**Because AI markets move faster than traditional software markets.** Model capabilities and prices change frequently, competitors launch quickly, and the only reliable way to learn what customers will pay for is to put a working product in their hands. A tight timeline forces the scope discipline that most failed MVPs lack.

## What Should Each Week of the 21-Day Sprint Include?

**Each week has a clear deliverable you can demo.** This is the plan we use for AI SaaS builds.

:::steps
### Week 1: Scope, Data Model and AI Prototype
Agree the single workflow and acceptance criteria. Design the data model, including tenants if you sell to companies. Build a working AI prototype on real sample data: prompts, retrieval, structured output and an evaluation set of example inputs with expected results.
---
### Week 2: Core Product and Billing
Build authentication, the core workflow screens and API, the retrieval pipeline and background jobs. Integrate Stripe Checkout and subscription webhooks, and add usage tracking per customer.
---
### Week 3: Hardening, Onboarding and Launch
Add error handling, retries, rate limits and monitoring. Build onboarding with sample data so new users see value immediately. Run the evaluation set again, fix quality gaps, deploy to production and hand over the code and documentation.
:::

:::warning
### The most common reason AI MVPs slip
Teams build the full interface before proving the AI step works on real data. If output quality is not good enough, the screens are wasted. Prove the AI in week one.
:::

## What Tech Stack Should You Use for an AI SaaS MVP?

**Use a stack that is fast to build with, cheap to run at low volume, and easy for future engineers and investors to understand.** This is a proven default:

| Layer | Recommended Choice | Why |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Frontend and API** | Next.js (React) with TypeScript | One codebase for UI and server routes, good SEO and a large hiring pool |
| **Database** | Managed PostgreSQL | Reliable, relational, and supports vector search through pgvector |
| **Vector search** | pgvector (start), dedicated vector database (later, if needed) | Avoids a second database until scale demands it |
| **AI models** | Hosted APIs from OpenAI, Anthropic or Google behind your own abstraction | Lets you swap or mix models as quality and pricing change |
| **Payments** | Stripe Checkout and Billing | Handles subscriptions, tax and invoices without custom payment code |
| **Background jobs** | A managed queue or job runner | Keeps long AI calls out of the request path |
| **Hosting** | Vercel or a similar managed platform | Zero server maintenance for a small team |

If your idea is a workflow tool for non-technical users and SEO is not important yet, a no-code build can also work. We compare both routes in [React / Next.js vs Bubble.io](/blog/react-vs-bubble-io-for-saas-mvp-2026).

## How Do You Protect Gross Margins in an AI SaaS?

**Treat model usage as a cost of goods sold and engineer it like one.** AI costs scale with usage, so pricing and architecture must account for them.

- **Cache** identical or near-identical requests and reuse embeddings instead of recomputing them.
- **Route by difficulty:** use a smaller, cheaper model for classification and extraction, and a stronger model only where reasoning quality matters.
- **Trim context:** send only the most relevant retrieved passages, not entire documents.
- **Cap usage per plan** and show customers their usage, so heavy users move to higher tiers.
- **Track cost per customer** from the first day, so pricing decisions are based on data.

For the strategy side of this (why some AI products retain users and others churn), read [AI wrapper vs defensible AI SaaS](/blog/ai-wrapper-vs-defensible-ai-saas-2026).

## How Does AI Compliance Differ in the USA, UK and UAE?

**The core principles are similar: know what personal data you process, minimise it, secure it and be transparent with users.** The details differ by market:

- **United States:** state privacy laws such as the CCPA/CPRA in California apply to many B2C products, HIPAA applies if you handle protected health information, and enterprise buyers often ask for SOC 2 reports.
- **United Kingdom:** UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018 apply, and the ICO publishes guidance on AI and data protection.
- **UAE:** the federal Personal Data Protection Law applies onshore, while free zones such as DIFC and ADGM have their own data protection regimes.

Check that your model providers' data processing terms suit your market, and avoid sending more personal data to models than the task needs. Our regional guides for the [UK](/blog/web-development-mvp-ecommerce-agency-uk-2026), [USA](/blog/saas-mvp-custom-crm-agency-usa-2026) and [UAE](/blog/web-ecommerce-crm-development-agency-dubai-uae-2026) go deeper.

## Frequently Asked Questions

:::faq
### Can you really build an AI SaaS MVP in 21 days?
Yes, if the scope is limited to one core workflow and the team uses managed services for authentication, payments and hosting. A senior team following a fixed weekly plan can launch a production-ready first version in about three weeks.
### What should not be included in a 21-day AI MVP?
Leave out secondary workflows, complex admin dashboards, native mobile apps, custom model training and most integrations beyond the one that delivers the core value. Add them after real customers have used the product.
### Do I need to train my own AI model for an MVP?
Usually not. Hosted models combined with retrieval over your customers' data and well-designed structured outputs are enough for most MVPs. Custom training only makes sense once you have proprietary data and a proven use case.
### What is the best database for an AI SaaS MVP?
Managed PostgreSQL with the pgvector extension is a strong default. It stores your relational data and vector embeddings in one place, which keeps the architecture simple until scale requires a dedicated vector database.
### Who owns the code after an agency builds my AI MVP?
You should. Make sure your contract transfers full ownership of the source code, data and infrastructure accounts to your company on delivery.

title: React / Next.js vs Bubble.io for Your SaaS MVP in 2026: Speed, Cost and Scale Compared
metaTitle: React / Next.js vs Bubble.io for a SaaS MVP (2026)
metaDescription: Should you build your SaaS MVP with Bubble.io or React and Next.js? Compare speed, long-term cost, SEO, scalability, code ownership and investor readiness.
excerpt: An honest comparison of Bubble.io and React/Next.js for SaaS MVPs: when no-code is the smarter choice, when custom code pays off, and how investors view each.

author: Muhammad Ahmad
authorBio: Muhammad Ahmad is the founder of WebMavien, a web and SaaS development agency. He has 8+ years of experience building React, Next.js and Bubble.io products and has delivered 100+ websites, MVPs and platforms for founders in the UK, USA and UAE.
content:
Choose Bubble.io for your SaaS MVP when you need to validate a workflow quickly and SEO, heavy data processing and complex integrations are not yet important. Choose React and Next.js when organic search, performance, complex logic, scalability or investor technical due diligence are part of your plan. Bubble.io is usually faster and cheaper to launch; Next.js is usually cheaper to scale and easier to own long term.

:::takeaways
### Key Takeaways
- **Bubble.io wins on speed to first launch** for workflow tools, internal apps and marketplaces.
- **React and Next.js win on SEO, performance, flexibility and ownership** of a standard codebase.
- **Long-term cost differs:** Bubble.io charges by platform usage (workload units), while custom code mainly costs hosting plus engineering time.
- **There is no wrong first choice,** only a wrong time to switch. Plan the trigger points in advance.
:::

## How Do React / Next.js and Bubble.io Compare?

**They are built for different stages and goals.** Bubble.io is a visual no-code platform that hosts your app for you. React is a JavaScript library for building interfaces, and Next.js is a React framework that adds server rendering, routing and API routes.

| Factor | Bubble.io | React / Next.js |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Speed to first launch** | Very fast for standard workflows | Fast with a senior team; slower for beginners |
| **Upfront build effort** | Lower | Higher |
| **Ongoing platform cost** | Usage-based (workload units) that grows with activity | Hosting and database costs, usually lower per user at scale |
| **SEO and page speed** | Limited control over rendering and Core Web Vitals | Full control: server rendering, static pages, image optimisation |
| **Complex logic and data** | Possible but harder to maintain visually | Unlimited, with standard testing tools |
| **Code ownership and portability** | Your app runs on Bubble's platform | You own a standard codebase you can host anywhere |
| **Hiring and handover** | Requires Bubble specialists | Draws on one of the largest developer communities |
| **Investor due diligence** | Accepted at pre-seed; sometimes questioned later | Easy to audit and hand to an engineering team |

## When Is Bubble.io the Smarter Choice?

**Bubble.io is the smarter choice when learning fast matters more than long-term scale.** It works best when:

- You are testing whether a workflow or marketplace idea has demand.
- Your first users come from sales, communities or partnerships rather than Google search.
- The app is mostly forms, lists, dashboards and standard workflows.
- You want to change features daily based on feedback without an engineering team.

Many successful products start on Bubble.io and migrate later. Our [MVP scoping and Bubble-to-Next.js migration guide](/blog/startup-mvp-scoping-and-bubble-to-nextjs-migration) explains when and how.

## When Should You Choose React and Next.js From Day One?

**Start with React and Next.js when your growth model or product depends on things no-code handles poorly.**

:::grid
### SEO Is a Core Channel
Content marketing, programmatic landing pages and marketplace listing pages rank better with server rendering and strong Core Web Vitals.
---
### Performance at Scale
Large datasets, real-time updates or heavy processing need control over queries, caching and infrastructure.
---
### Complex Integrations or AI
Multi-step AI pipelines, custom APIs and many third-party integrations are easier to build, test and maintain in code.
---
### You Plan to Raise or Be Acquired
A standard, documented codebase simplifies technical due diligence and hiring an in-house team.
:::

:::tip
### A hybrid approach often works
Some teams launch the application on Bubble.io and build the marketing site and SEO pages in Next.js from day one. That keeps validation fast while building organic traffic in parallel.
:::

## Which Option Costs Less Over Three Years?

**It depends on usage. Bubble.io usually costs less in the first months; custom code usually costs less as usage and complexity grow.** On Bubble.io, platform fees rise with workload, and complex features can take longer to build as the app grows. With Next.js, the upfront build costs more, but hosting is relatively inexpensive at scale and any engineer familiar with React can extend the product.

To compare fairly, estimate three things for each option: the cost of the first build, monthly platform or hosting costs at your expected usage in year two, and the engineering effort for the features on your roadmap. See [what drives SaaS development cost](/blog/saas-application-development-cost-2026) for the full list of cost factors.

## How Do Investors View Bubble.io vs Custom Code?

**At pre-seed, investors care far more about traction than about your stack.** A no-code MVP with paying customers beats a custom-coded product with none. From seed and Series A onwards, technical due diligence becomes more common, and investors may ask how the product will scale, who owns the code and how quickly an engineering team can work on it. A clear migration plan answers those questions even if you are still on Bubble.io.

:::casestudy

## Frequently Asked Questions

:::faq
### Is Bubble.io good for building a SaaS MVP?
Yes. Bubble.io is well suited to validating SaaS workflows, internal tools and marketplaces quickly. It is less suited to products that depend on SEO, heavy data processing or complex integrations.
### Is Next.js better than Bubble.io for SEO?
Yes. Next.js supports server-side rendering and static generation, fine control over metadata and strong Core Web Vitals, which give it a clear advantage for search-driven growth.
### Can I move from Bubble.io to Next.js later?
Yes. Data can be exported through Bubble's Data API, and the product can be rebuilt in stages using the strangler pattern so customers experience no downtime.
### Do investors accept no-code MVPs?
At pre-seed, most investors focus on traction rather than the tech stack. Later rounds may involve technical due diligence, where a documented migration plan or custom codebase helps.
### Which is faster to build: Bubble.io or Next.js?
Bubble.io is usually faster for standard workflows. A senior Next.js team can still launch a focused MVP in about three to four weeks, with a codebase that does not need to be rebuilt later.
:::

content:
To choose the right web development agency, check five things: relevant work with measurable results, senior engineers who will actually build your project, a written scope with a fixed timeline, full ownership of your code and accounts, and clear support after launch. Speak to at least one past client, and compare proposals against the same scope rather than on price alone.

:::takeaways
### Key Takeaways
- **Relevant results beat a pretty portfolio.** Look for projects like yours with outcomes you can verify.
- **Know who builds your project.** Ask for the engineers' names and experience, not only the sales team's.
- **Insist on a written scope, timeline and code ownership** before any payment.
- **Red flags** include vague estimates, no references, pressure to sign quickly and agencies that keep your hosting or code.
:::

## Why Does Your Choice of Agency Matter So Much?

**Your website is often the first and last thing a customer checks before buying.** A slow, generic or broken site loses sales and search rankings every day, while a well-built one generates leads around the clock. Choosing the wrong agency usually costs far more than the initial project fee: missed launch dates, a rebuild and lost revenue.

## Should You Choose a Custom Website or a Template?

**Templates suit simple brochure sites on a tight timeline; custom builds suit businesses that need performance, unique functionality or long-term growth.**

| Factor | Template / Theme | Custom-Built Website |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Launch speed** | Fastest | Fast with an experienced team |
| **Design uniqueness** | Shared with many other sites | Built around your brand |
| **Performance and SEO** | Often slowed by unused code and plugins | Optimised for speed and search from the start |
| **Custom features** | Limited by plugins | Built to your requirements |
| **Long-term cost** | Plugin and theme renewals add up | Lower ongoing dependency on third parties |

## What 7 Qualities Should You Look For in a Web Development Agency?

:::steps
### Proven, Relevant Results
Case studies in your industry or with similar features, including outcomes such as more leads, sales or users.
---
### Senior Engineers on Your Project
Experienced developers make fewer architecture mistakes and move faster than junior teams learning on your budget.
---
### A Clear, Written Process
A defined sequence from discovery to design, build, testing and launch, with demos along the way.
---
### Fixed Scope and Timeline
A written list of what will be delivered, with acceptance criteria and a delivery date.
---
### Full Code and Account Ownership
You own the source code, design files, domain, hosting and every third-party account.
---
### SEO and Performance Built In
Fast pages, clean structure, metadata, structured data and analytics should be part of the build, not an expensive extra.
---
### Support After Launch
A defined support window and a clear way to request fixes and new features.
:::

## Should Your Agency Build With React or Bubble.io?

**It depends on your goals.** React and Next.js are best for websites and apps that need speed, SEO and complex features. Bubble.io is a strong option for validating web applications and marketplaces quickly without a large budget. A good agency explains the trade-offs and recommends one honestly. See our full [React / Next.js vs Bubble.io comparison](/blog/react-vs-bubble-io-for-saas-mvp-2026).

## How Do You Evaluate an Agency's Portfolio and Reviews?

**Look past the screenshots.** Open live projects and test them on your phone. Check page speed with Google PageSpeed Insights. Read reviews on independent platforms such as Clutch or Google, and look for detailed reviews that mention specific results. Finally, ask to speak with a past client, ideally one whose project resembles yours.

## What Red Flags Should You Watch For?

:::warning
### Walk away if you see these
- An estimate given before the agency understands your requirements.
- No written scope or acceptance criteria.
- No verifiable case studies or client references.
- The agency keeps ownership of your code, domain or hosting.
- Pressure to sign quickly with large upfront payments and no milestones.
- Vague answers about who will build the project and how progress is shared.
:::

## How Should You Compare Agency Proposals?

**Compare like with like.** Send every agency the same brief, then compare proposals on scope coverage, timeline, team seniority, ownership terms, support and evidence of results, not on headline price alone. A cheaper quote that leaves out testing, SEO or support often costs more in the end. If you are building a software product rather than a website, read [what drives SaaS development cost](/blog/saas-application-development-cost-2026) and our guide to [choosing an MVP development agency](/blog/mvp-development-agency-for-startups-21-days).

## How Does a 21-Day Website Delivery Model Work?

**A 21-day delivery model splits the project into three focused weeks with a fixed scope.** Week one covers strategy, structure and design; week two covers development; week three covers content, testing, SEO setup and launch. It works because scope is agreed in writing up front and senior engineers do the work. Learn more about [our process](/process).

## Frequently Asked Questions

:::faq
### How do I choose a good web development agency?
Look for relevant case studies with measurable results, senior engineers assigned to your project, a written scope and timeline, full ownership of your code and accounts, and defined post-launch support. Always speak to at least one past client.
### What questions should I ask a web development agency?
Ask who will build the project, what exactly is in scope, how changes are handled, who owns the code and accounts, what happens after launch, and whether you can speak to a past client.
### How long does it take to build a website?
A focused business website or web application can be launched in about 3 to 4 weeks with a fixed scope and an experienced team. Larger platforms with many integrations take longer.
### Is a custom website better than a template?
A custom website is better when performance, SEO, unique features or long-term growth matter. Templates are adequate for simple brochure sites that need to launch quickly.
### Should I hire a local web development agency?
Location matters less than communication, time-zone overlap and proven results. Many businesses work successfully with remote agencies that offer regular calls and shared progress updates.
